maria: Heads up — we had two H100 nodes (p3-12) do a hard restart during overnight FP8 soak with long-context KV churn. No OOM in host, NVML shows 'GPU_RESET', dmesg has pci-errors. Anyone seen this pattern before?
chris: Hmm. GPU_RESET + pci-errors usually points at DMA/PCIe issues. Does the trace show sustained PCIe traffic spikes when KV evictions happen?
alex: Can you paste the small perf snippet you grabbed? even just the hot kernel names + timestamps.
maria: Pasted quick log: 
```
[2026-03-16T04:12:03Z] kernel: nvlink0: pcie timeout
[2026-03-16T04:12:03Z] nvml: GPU 2 reset detected
[2026-03-16T04:12:03Z] runtime: launch kernel transformer_te_fft_large (0x7f3a...)
[2026-03-16T04:12:03Z] runtime: kv_replay_eviction flush 128MB
[2026-03-16T04:12:03Z] perf: pcie_bw util 98%  avg_qsize 18
```
Not super verbose but you can see kernel + eviction spike right before reset.
sam: Two thoughts: 1) TE sometimes picks a larger FFT-style kernel for FP8 that heavily touches device memory + DMA; 2) Our batching heuristic ramps microbatch size on observed latency headroom which multiplies PCIe transfers when KV miss rate is high. Combined = bandwidth storm.
chris: Agree. I ran a synthetic repro locally: create loop with random KV churn + growing microbatch. Repro is reliable. Backtrace shows driver call stuck in nvme/pci submit before reset: 
```
#0 0x7f8a... in dma_submit()
#1 0x7f9b... transformer_te_fft_large
#2 0x7fcd... kernel_launch
#3 0x7fde... runtime_infer
```
alex: Quick mitigation: force TE to prefer the 'small' kernel family and cap microbatch tokens. Try env: `TE_FORCE_SMALL_KERNEL=1` + runtime config `max_tokens_per_microbatch=32`. That reduced peak BW in my local smoke.
maria: Trying that now on canary queue (2 nodes). Also enabling pci_bandwidth telemetry: `telemetry.pcie_sample_rate=100ms`. Will run a controlled KV churn script. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: Perf snapshot uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/capture/3412345678/canary-01 (flamegraph + pcie timeline)
sam: If canary looks good, add router guard to avoid increasing microbatch when recent PCIe util > 85% and KV eviction rate high. Also add automatic fallback to INT8 kernels if repeated resets occur.
maria: Canary ran 45 minutes. With TE_FORCE_SMALL_KERNEL + max_tokens_per_microbatch=32 we saw peak pcie_util ~62% and no resets. Without changes it peaked 99% and reset at ~12min. I'll open a small PR for the guard and a short rollout plan.
chris: Good. PR should include repro script and a unit test for the batching throttle logic. Also add an anecdotal note in the kernel selector about bandwidth-sensitive kernels.
maria: PR #4621 opened: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/4621 — includes telemetry, canary results, and suggested rollback steps. I'll shepherd the canary to prod after a 24h soak.
deploy-bot: canary started: id=canary-3412345678-1, nodes=[p3-12-07,p3-12-08], policy=canary-small-kernel, expires=2026-03-17T12:40:00Z
amended: Next steps: add max_tokens_per_microbatch default to 32 for H100 when fp8_enabled=true, and create a regression alert for PCIe util > 90% + reset event.
alex: Thanks team — this feels like a good pattern: kernel-family choice + batching throttle + telemetry alerting. Keep updates here and ping @oncall if any prod escalations.
